title: Nominal Prices, Retail Investor Participation, and Return Momentum
authors: Jun Jie Du; Dashan Huang; Yu-Jane Liu; Yushui Shi; Avanidhar Subrahmanyam; Huacheng Zhang
eligible_reason: The main identification is cross-sectional (Fama-MacBeth momentum by nominal-price quintile, Tables 2-7, 10), but the main-text stock-split analysis (Tables 8-9, Figures 4-5) is a staggered event-window DiD: Chinese A-share stocks that split, each observed from 6 months before to 6 months after its split month, after = 1 in months 1-6 after the split; splits occur in many calendar months (35-38 distinct first-split months for 2016-2020 in Table 8; 184-189 for 2000-2020 in Table 9). reghdfe y after if dummyh==h ..., absorb(stkcd month) cluster(stkcd month), no controls, separately for high- and non-high-priced stocks; Figures 4-5 are the matching unstacked event studies with relative-month dummies. Only split stocks are in the sample (no never-treated), so comparisons are with not-yet-split stocks, as in mnsc.2021.01740. Qualifying: Table 8 FE columns without amountadj (4), Table 9 FE columns without amountadj (2), Figure 4 (2 paths), Figure 5 (2 paths). Excluded: noabsorb columns (no FE) and amountadj columns (split ratio x after, treatment intensity).
design_notes: Stata reghdfe for Tables 8-9 and Figures 4-5 (SAS for most other tables). Each table/figure folder ships its own processed dataset; shipped data reproduce the published N (10,470 and 11,317 in Table 8; 43,154 and 41,748 in Table 9, per the authors' logs). Sample restriction countn >= 10 keeps events with at least 10 window months; in Table 9 countn is computed after keeping dummyh and 2000-2020, in Table 8 and Figures before the year restriction. Event studies omit both n = -6 and n = 0 (needed with treated-only samples). Table 7 regresses holdings on continuous log price; Table 6 is a cross-sectional comparison; appendix Table IB10 is a PSM treat_post design (appendix-only, matching).
main_or_robustness: main text, secondary analysis (validation test of the retail-participation channel)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Distinct first-split months among high-priced stocks, Table 8 sample (2016-2020); 38 for non-high; 184/189 in the Table 9 sample (2000-2020).
treatment_switches_off_note: Only across repeated split events of the same stock (later event windows code after = 0).

specs.treatment_definition: after = 1 in the six months following the stock's split month (n = 1..6); 0 for n = -6..0
specs.sample_condition: dummyh == 1 (high-priced stocks) & year(month) in 2016-2020; events with at least 10 window months (bysort stkcd annodt: countn >= 10)
specs.reported_location: Table 8, outreg2 column 2 (small investors, high-priced, stock and month FE)
specs.notes: Event-window panel of split stocks only (months -6..+6 around each split, n = 0 coded after = 0); identification from staggered split dates (not-yet-split stocks as controls), no never-treated stocks. FE stkcd (not stock x event): 147/685 (high) and 113/781 (non-high) stocks in the Table 8 sample have several split events, producing duplicate stkcd-month rows and treatment switch-offs across events; for CSA/BJS either use first split per stock (drop later-event rows, Hull fn. 6) or define the unit as stkcd x annodt (recorded deviation).

data_files_note: Processed event-window datasets shipped per table/figure (stksplit_par.dta 26,122 rows, 1,768 stocks; stksplit_mom.dta 92,436 rows, 3,142 stocks). Raw CSMAR/brokerage inputs are licensed/proprietary but the processed files needed for Tables 8-9 and Figures 4-5 are included.
data_provenance_note: Processed real data (CSMAR prices/splits; small/large investor holdings derived from brokerage accounts); row counts match the authors' logs.
software_notes: SAS 9.4 for data construction and most tables; Stata for Tables 8-9, Figures 4-5.
screener_notes: Screened from package, per-table readmes, logs and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Table column numbers are outreg2 output order; check the published table layout. Unit choice for repeated splits (stkcd vs stkcd x annodt) needs a lead decision.
